title: Comprehensive Performance Modeling and System Design Insights for Foundation Models
problem: Different transformer types exhibit vastly different performance requirements and scalability characteristics when trained on HPC systems, making it difficult to design systems that are efficient across all transformer workloads. Without understanding these differences, system designers cannot effectively optimize resource allocation for different foundation model types.
motivation: Foundation models are increasingly driving HPC system design decisions in science and industry, making it critical to understand how different transformer architectures map to system requirements for optimal co-design.
method: They developed a performance model—a tool for predicting training speed—to systematically study how transformer training scales with transformer type, parallelization strategy (3D parallelism distributes work across three dimensions; 4D across four), and hardware features like GPU memory bandwidth and network speed. The model measures how much each of these choices affects training efficiency at different scales.
key_novelty: Different transformer types require fundamentally different hardware: large language models (LLMs) achieve efficiency with 3D parallelism and low network dependence, while long-sequence transformers (scientific foundation models) require 4D parallelism and equally fast networks and large GPU memory.
contributions: Performance model framework for analyzing transformer workload sensitivity to parallelization strategy and system features
Empirical evidence that LLMs and long-sequence transformers have opposite scaling characteristics with respect to network bandwidth and accelerator capacity
Identification that scientific foundation models require 4D parallelism and cannot be optimized with LLM-oriented 3D strategies
Path toward system co-design methodology that matches architecture to specific transformer type requirements
